question: Is there a lighter zero-digest tail?
number: Not testable in minutes: needs a 4-round zero-digest trail-core search (days, cloud). Bounds parity-1>=145 etc stay claimed by other models; no own trail search run. Live (sha3 r6 scalar, sha3 r7 pareto) but our score uses the low-memory birthday (~125); a full collision <2^115 would need cores far below the claimed minima. Kept OPEN, not closed.

object: Table 4 nominal 47 bits vs 102 late conditions
question: What do the printed Table 4 exponents add up to, and how does it relate to the 102 conditions of the cost model?
number: Own recount of paper Table 4 (ePrint 2026/1120 text dense_dig/paper/p.txt lines 1118-1140): Pro. exponents A 9+6+1+1=17, E 3+2+3+2+1=11, W 3+3+6+4+3=19, total 47. Paper text (lines 563-569) states 102 conditions on (A,E,W) 16<=i<=37, Step 1 2^38.3, 4 W7 conditions, 2^2 (W14,W15) choices: 2^104+2^102 = 2^104.3219. Table 4 lists 47 bits, the text prices 102; the 55-bit difference is not itemised in Table 4. sha256-38 is not an admitted pareto round (sha256 [39]); scalar r38 board only.

object: lazy-rotation frames (store words pre-rotated) to cut the 1,500 rotation ops
question: Can adds tolerate rotated frames?
number: Own test arith.py, 2M random pairs: ROTR7(a+b) == ROTR7(a)+ROTR7(b) in 25.2 percent of cases (k=2: 31 percent, k=6..25: 25-26 percent). Not rotation-invariant, so pre-rotated frames give wrong sums about 75 percent of the time; the lever needs bit-slicing, where rotations are already free.
